body_ar: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين، وأصلي وأسلم على من بعث رحمة للعالمين، وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن اهتدى بهديه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين، السلام عليكم ورحمة الله تعالى وبركاته، أما بعد فقد سبق أن مواضع المخارج خمسة، الجوف والحلق واللسان والشفتان والخيشوم، فهذه خمسة مواضع هي محال الضغط على الهواء المنطلق من الرئة، وفي كل مكان ضغط عليه يتركب مخرج من مخارج الحروف، وقد سبق أن العلماء اختلفوا في عدد مخارج الحروف إلى أربعة أقوال: القول الأول قول الخليل بن أحمد الفراهيدي أنها سبعة عشر، وهو اختيار ابن الجزري، القول الثاني أنها تسعة وعشرين أي أن لكل حرف مخرجا
body_en:
In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Compassionate. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. I invoke blessings and peace upon him who was sent as a mercy to the worlds, and upon his family and his Companions and whoever has taken his guidance for guidance and his sunnah for a way, until the Day of Judgement. Peace be upon you, and the mercy of God, be He exalted, and His blessings.

To proceed: it has already been established that the locations of the points of articulation are five — the cavity, the throat, the tongue, the two lips and the nasal passage. These are five locations, and they are the places where pressure is applied to the air issuing from the lung; and at every place where it is pressed, one of the points of articulation of the letters is formed. It has also already been established that the scholars differed over the number of the points of articulation of the letters, into four positions. The first position is that of al-Khalil ibn Ahmad al-Farahidi, that they are seventeen, and this is what Ibn al-Jazari chose. The second position is that they are twenty-nine, that is, that every letter has a point of articulation of its own

The published page carries only the opening excerpt of this tape; the Arabic breaks off and the full text is offered on the site as a downloadable Word document. The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends. Nothing has been supplied to complete it.

The Sheikh announces four positions on the number of the points of articulation and the excerpt gives only the first two before breaking off mid-clause. The remaining two are not in the source; nothing has been supplied for them, and the English must not be read as a complete statement of the disagreement.
The Sheikh reports that Ibn al-Jazari chose al-Khalil's position; he does not state his own preference in this excerpt, and none has been supplied.

al-Jazariyyah is the versified primer on Qur'anic recitation by Ibn al-Jazari, and 'the author' throughout this series is Ibn al-Jazari. The series title is left transliterated and untranslated. Articles 436-446 are tapes of this one series; their tape numbering in the titles does not run in the same order as the article IDs.
